scope: Seven original proposed Tourmelloh journeys; existing four expanded and three short standalone routes added.
method: Research preceded writing. Agent Reach Exa discovered official pages; one Exa query hit a free-tier HTTP 429, so built-in web search continued discovery. Jina Reader recovered the supplied Satvik reference. Official district, state tourism, monument, temple and UNESCO sources govern factual visit notes. No competitor prose or unverified service claims were transferred.
status: Proposed itinerary sequence. No inventory, hotel, service, fare or booking is confirmed by these files.

The arrangements.included key is a UI contract: its public heading must say To specify in your quote, not Confirmed inclusions.

routeContent.lead: A suggested four-day introduction to Kashi, with three nights in Varanasi. Spend a morning on the Ganga, give the old city and Kashi Vishwanath their own time, and set aside a separate day for Sarnath. The route leaves space for breakfast, rest and the practical work of moving through a busy pilgrimage city.
routeContent.pace: One base; early starts balanced with afternoon breaks
routeContent.bestFor: A first visit to Varanasi, a family pilgrimage, or travellers who want the river and the old city without changing hotels.
routeContent.season: October to March is the most comfortable general window for outdoor exploring. Winter fog can affect river views; festival dates call for a different crowd and transport plan.
highlights: A Ganga morning, by boat or on foot
Kashi Vishwanath and the old-city lanes
Sarnath, Dhamek Stupa and the museum
Three nights in the same Varanasi base

dayPlans.title: Arrive, settle in, meet the river
dayPlans.description: Keep your first day centred on arrival and one riverfront experience. Dashashwamedh Ghat is the proposed evening focus; the timing depends on your connection and the final approach to your accommodation. A late arrival simply moves aarti to another evening.
moments: Settle into your Varanasi base
An introduction to the ghats
Evening Ganga aarti, if arrival allows

schedule.title: Leave room to arrive properly
schedule.text: Allow time to reach your chosen accommodation, eat and rest. If you stay in the old city, establish the vehicle drop-off point and the last stretch on foot before travelling. Keep any long temple circuit off this first afternoon.

schedule.title: Find your way to Dashashwamedh
schedule.text: Approach the river before the evening ceremony rather than arriving at its busiest moment. Use a short walk to understand the steps, meeting point and return route. A ground-level viewing plan should suit the group before considering a boat.

schedule.title: Watch aarti, then call it a day
schedule.text: Stay for Ganga aarti when the arrival schedule permits, then return for dinner. Choose a position from which the group can watch comfortably, with a clear route back through the lanes afterwards. Leave time for dinner and an easy return before tomorrow's early start.

dayPlans.travel: Arrival transfer to be matched to your actual airport or station and accommodation address.
dayPlans.walking: Ghat approaches involve steps. Choose a short first walk and discuss a suitable viewing position if standing or stairs are difficult.

dayPlans.title: The Ganga at first light, then Kashi Vishwanath
dayPlans.description: Use the cooler part of the day for the river, then give the temple and surrounding lanes a separate block of time. The boat and darshan sequence can change with conditions; breakfast and a proper rest are part of the proposed day, not gaps to fill with extra stops.
moments: First light along the river
Kashi Vishwanath, with time for security
A short old-city walk and an afternoon break

schedule.title: See the ghats from the water or shore
schedule.text: Consider a short Ganga boat ride when conditions and local permissions allow. Confirm the boarding ghat, life jackets and duration before agreeing to it. A riverfront walk is the alternative, with the turnaround point chosen for your comfort rather than a target number of ghats.

schedule.title: Make time for the temple
schedule.text: After breakfast, visit Kashi Vishwanath if darshan is part of your journey. Its current rules prohibit phones and other electronic devices, so settle storage before joining the entry queue. Give the visit its own block of time, including security, darshan and the return through the surrounding lanes.

schedule.title: Explore a little, then pause
schedule.text: Choose a manageable stretch of the old-city lanes and a stop for tea before returning to rest. Later, revisit a ghat you liked or use this evening for aarti if you missed it on arrival. An interest in Banarasi textiles can shape the afternoon's shopping stop.

dayPlans.travel: Local journeys only. Vehicle access, walking approaches and any boat departure point need confirming for the day.
dayPlans.walking: Steps, uneven riverfront surfaces and standing in temple queues. Shorten the ghat walk independently of the temple visit.

dayPlans.title: Sarnath: the stupa, the museum, the wider story
dayPlans.description: Give Sarnath a substantial part of the day rather than treating it as a brief photo stop. Its archaeological remains and museum tell different parts of the story of the Buddha's first teaching. If today is Friday, exchange this day with the Varanasi day when the museum is a priority.
moments: Dhamek Stupa and the archaeological remains
The museum's Lion Capital of Ashoka
A relaxed final evening in Varanasi

schedule.title: Start with the archaeological site
schedule.text: Travel out after breakfast and focus first on Dhamek Stupa and the excavated remains around it. Allow time to understand what you are looking at rather than moving rapidly between monuments. A guided visit can connect the surviving stupa and ruins with the history of the Buddha's first teaching.

schedule.title: See the objects behind the history
schedule.text: Visit Sarnath Museum on an open day, with the Lion Capital of Ashoka as a key object to look for. Museum entry and the outdoor site are separate visits. Check the current opening hours before setting the order, and leave a break for lunch between them.

schedule.title: Return without another long excursion
schedule.text: Head back to Varanasi with time to rest and pack. If you still want a final riverfront visit, choose one familiar ghat and keep the evening local. An additional monastery in Sarnath can replace some free time, subject to its own visitor arrangements.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: about 45–75 minutes each way to Sarnath from a central Varanasi base; traffic and the exact address can change this.
dayPlans.walking: Outdoor paths at the archaeological site and time on your feet in museum galleries; plan shade and breaks around the weather.

dayPlans.title: A final morning, shaped around your departure
dayPlans.description: The final day protects your onward connection. A later departure may leave time for breakfast and one nearby stop; an early departure is simply a transfer day. Keep luggage collection and the route out of the old city in mind before agreeing to any last visit.
moments: Breakfast or a familiar ghat, if time allows
Check out and collect your belongings
Continue from your confirmed departure point

schedule.title: Repeat something you enjoyed
schedule.text: If your departure leaves enough room, return to a nearby stretch of river or linger over breakfast. Choose somewhere close to your accommodation. This is a chance to revisit a favourite place, rather than start a new cross-city sightseeing circuit.

schedule.title: Leave time for the last stretch
schedule.text: Check the accommodation's checkout arrangements and where your onward vehicle can meet you. Collect any belongings held in storage and build the transfer around the exact station or airport on your ticket. Different Varanasi railway stations should never be treated as interchangeable.

schedule.title: Continue with a clear departure plan
schedule.text: Your flight or train determines the remaining time. Collect your luggage and set the transfer around the reporting time, with a comfortable margin for the journey out of the city. If you want a further destination, extend the route instead of squeezing it into this morning.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart Varanasi
dayPlans.travel: Departure transfer allowance to be set from your actual ticket, hotel address and local traffic advice.
dayPlans.walking: Optional short walk only; the day can be planned entirely around breakfast and departure.

planningNotes.title: Choose your base for access, not just the view
planningNotes.text: Three nights are proposed in Varanasi. Before choosing a riverfront or old-city stay, ask about vehicle access, steps, lifts and the distance from the drop-off point. This itinerary does not certify any property as accessible.

planningNotes.title: Protect the Sarnath museum visit
planningNotes.text: The museum closes on Fridays. Keep days two and three interchangeable until the travel dates are known, and reconfirm the museum's current hours rather than relying on a fixed clock time in a sample itinerary.

planningNotes.title: Keep temple and river arrangements separate
planningNotes.text: Kashi Vishwanath currently prohibits electronic devices inside. Check the official instructions close to your visit. Boat operations depend on river conditions and local restrictions; boating, darshan passes and aarti viewing arrangements need their own confirmation.

planningNotes.title: Read the travel times as planning allowances
planningNotes.text: The local transfer range is an editorial estimate for organising the day, not a live traffic prediction. The final address, crowd controls, weather and your chosen transport can change it. Dates and needs come before a fixed timetable.

Arrival, departure and Sarnath transport: vehicle and pickup points
Guiding, admission tickets and the exact sightseeing scope
Any river outing or temple service, priced and confirmed separately
excluded: Flights or rail tickets unless specifically added
Meals and drinks outside the agreed meal plan
Ritual offerings, personal shopping and gratuities
Any activity or access arrangement absent from the written quote

routeContent.lead: A suggested six-day pilgrimage route with three nights in Varanasi, one in Prayagraj and one in Ayodhya. Give Kashi Vishwanath and Sarnath separate days, pause at the Sangam, then continue to Ram Mandir and the Sarayu. Overnight stops keep the two intercity journeys from becoming a single exhausting sightseeing day.
routeContent.pace: Three bases; two intercity journeys; temple queues and rest time
routeContent.bestFor: Families combining Kashi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, especially when the purpose of the trip is more important than the number of temples visited.
routeContent.season: October to March is a useful starting window for this northern-plains route. Plan major religious dates separately, with more allowance for crowds, altered access and transport delays.
highlights: Three nights for Varanasi and Sarnath
A dedicated overnight stop in Prayagraj
The Sangam and the Sarayu riverfront
An Ayodhya morning centred on your chosen darshan

dayPlans.title: Arrive in Kashi, without a temple marathon
dayPlans.description: Your arrival time sets the first day's programme. Settle into Varanasi before approaching the river, with evening aarti as the main possible outing. There are two further evenings here, so a delayed connection does not mean you have missed the experience.
moments: Arrive at your Varanasi base
Locate the riverfront approach
Aarti if the arrival leaves enough time

schedule.title: Check the last part of the journey
schedule.text: Reach your selected accommodation and leave time for a meal and rest. Establish where a vehicle can stop and whether luggage has to travel the final stretch separately. This matters particularly when a riverside location is chosen for a group with older travellers.

schedule.title: A manageable introduction to the ghats
schedule.text: Choose a short approach towards Dashashwamedh Ghat. Identify the meeting place and a comfortable viewing position before the evening becomes busy. Discuss steps and standing time now rather than assuming everyone in the group will use the same vantage point.

schedule.title: Let aarti be the day's focus
schedule.text: Watch the Ganga ceremony if your arrival permits, then return for dinner. If the journey has been tiring, move it to another evening. Choose a viewing position and return route around the group's comfort, with a little time by the water before heading back.

dayPlans.travel: Arrival transfer planned from your actual airport or station to the selected accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: A short riverfront approach with ghat steps; shorten or omit it according to the group's needs.

dayPlans.title: A proper day for Kashi Vishwanath
dayPlans.description: Put the visit that matters most at the centre of the day. For many families that is Kashi Vishwanath. Keep its entry process separate from an optional river outing, and leave space for breakfast, waiting and a return to the accommodation between excursions.
moments: Kashi Vishwanath darshan planning
An optional Ganga morning
Old-city lanes at a comfortable pace

schedule.title: Build the morning around darshan
schedule.text: Choose the temple visit around the current official arrangements. Phones and electronic devices are prohibited inside, so decide where belongings will be stored before joining a queue. Give security, darshan and the return through the surrounding lanes a generous share of the morning.

schedule.title: Breakfast, a short walk, then rest
schedule.text: After the temple visit, take a meal break and explore a small section of the old city if the group wishes. Keep the return route straightforward. Avoid adding several distant temples merely because a vehicle is available; another full Varanasi day follows tomorrow.

schedule.title: Choose the river experience you want
schedule.text: Use the evening for aarti if it was missed on arrival, or take a shorter riverfront walk. A boat trip can instead be discussed for an early-morning slot when conditions permit. Decide its timing and boarding arrangements independently of the temple queue.

dayPlans.travel: Local travel with the final temple approach set by current access controls.
dayPlans.walking: Standing in queues and walking through busy lanes; plan a rest after the main temple visit.

dayPlans.title: Sarnath before the route moves on
dayPlans.description: Sarnath introduces the Buddhist history of this region before the journey turns towards Prayagraj. Keep the visit concentrated on the archaeological site and museum, with time to return, rest and prepare for tomorrow's change of city.
moments: Dhamek Stupa and excavated remains
Sarnath Museum on an open day
A final night in the Varanasi base

schedule.title: Go beyond the riverfront
schedule.text: Leave after breakfast for Sarnath, associated with the Buddha's first teaching. Spend time around Dhamek Stupa and the archaeological remains. This is a different kind of visit from a temple queue, so allow time for explanation, looking and pauses outdoors.

schedule.title: See the museum's collection
schedule.text: On an open day, explore the museum and look for the Lion Capital of Ashoka. Friday is its weekly closure, so the second and third days may need exchanging. Choose a lunch break before returning rather than filling the remaining time with every nearby monastery.

schedule.title: Prepare for the first intercity leg
schedule.text: Return to Varanasi, check tomorrow's departure arrangements and have an easy evening. Confirm any essential medicines, luggage handling and meal-stop preferences with your travelling companions. If a final ghat visit matters, keep it nearby and preserve time to rest.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: 45–75 minutes each way between central Varanasi and Sarnath, subject to your address and traffic.
dayPlans.walking: Outdoor archaeological paths and museum galleries; the number of stops can be reduced without changing the overnight plan.

dayPlans.title: To Prayagraj, with time at the Sangam
dayPlans.description: Travel after breakfast and make Prayagraj an overnight stop. The Sangam, where the Ganga and Yamuna meet and the Saraswati belongs to sacred tradition, is the principal visit. This day deliberately avoids continuing to Ayodhya after sightseeing.
moments: Travel to your Prayagraj base
Visit the Sangam riverfront
A possible boat outing, subject to conditions

schedule.title: A transfer with a break
schedule.text: Check out and travel towards Prayagraj, allowing time for a comfort stop and the final approach into the city. The estimated road allowance is for planning only. Set the departure around the group's breakfast and rest needs rather than treating it as a race to the next monument.

schedule.title: Give the Sangam your attention
schedule.text: After settling in and eating, head towards the confluence. Boats can take visitors towards the meeting of the rivers when local conditions permit; confirm the operator, boarding arrangements and safety equipment before deciding. A riverbank visit remains a valid alternative.

schedule.title: Leave personal rituals their own time
schedule.text: If a ceremony is the purpose of your visit, plan it explicitly with time and costs agreed separately. Otherwise, return for a quiet evening. For an interest in modern Indian history, discuss Anand Bhawan, the Nehru family house museum, as an alternative visit when opening hours and the arrival time fit.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: roughly 3–4 hours by road from Varanasi, including a short break; traffic, stopping points and festival controls can add time.
dayPlans.walking: Riverbank surfaces and boat boarding can be uneven. Discuss access before choosing a boat or a ritual location.

dayPlans.title: Continue to Ayodhya and the Sarayu
dayPlans.description: Make the move to Ayodhya the main task of the morning. After checking in, use the evening for Ram Ki Paidi and the Sarayu riverfront. Keep the main temple programme for tomorrow, unless your confirmed departure requires a different sequence.
moments: Travel to Ayodhya
Settle in before further sightseeing
Ram Ki Paidi and the Sarayu

schedule.title: Travel with a realistic arrival window
schedule.text: Leave Prayagraj after breakfast, with a rest stop built into the road journey. Confirm the approach to your Ayodhya accommodation before setting an exact arrival time. Lunch and a break come first, leaving the riverfront outing for the more comfortable part of the afternoon or evening.

schedule.title: Settle in and prepare for darshan
schedule.text: Eat, rest and confirm the next day's temple entry arrangements. Agree which visit takes priority and how the group wants to handle walking and queues. If tomorrow's onward connection is early, rearrange the programme or add a night instead of promising several visits before departure.

schedule.title: Spend time at Ram Ki Paidi
schedule.text: Visit the series of ghats beside the Sarayu for a riverfront introduction to Ayodhya. The length of the walk should follow the group's energy after travelling. If a ceremony is part of the current evening programme, choose whether to stay before returning for dinner.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: around 4–5 hours by road from Prayagraj with a short stop. The actual route and city access need checking for your date.
dayPlans.walking: Keep this to a short riverfront walk after the transfer; steps and the distance from the drop-off point should be discussed.

dayPlans.title: Ayodhya's temples, then your onward journey
dayPlans.description: Choose an onward connection that leaves a meaningful window for your principal temple visit. Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi and Kanak Bhawan should not become a compulsory checklist. The order follows current access arrangements, the group's religious priorities and its ability to manage stairs and waiting.
moments: Ram Mandir as the main proposed visit
Hanuman Garhi or Kanak Bhawan if suitable
Depart from your confirmed Ayodhya connection

schedule.title: Put the main darshan first in the plan
schedule.text: Set the morning around the Ram Mandir visit if that is the reason for travelling. Check official entry instructions and allow a generous queue window. A later onward connection leaves room for the visit, a meal and a comfortable return for luggage.

schedule.title: Choose a second temple deliberately
schedule.text: Hanuman Garhi involves a steep stepped approach; decide whether it suits the group before adding it. Kanak Bhawan is another possible visit in the temple area. Choose according to your interests and available time rather than trying to fit both into a short departure morning.

schedule.title: Finish without a rushed transfer
schedule.text: Return for luggage and travel to the airport or railway station on your ticket. Choose a later connection or an additional Ayodhya night when the main darshan needs more time. Any further journey to Lucknow is a separate transfer to plan and quote.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart Ayodhya
dayPlans.travel: Final transfer depends on the specific Ayodhya airport or station; a Lucknow departure requires a separate road allowance.
dayPlans.walking: Temple approaches, queues and substantial stairs at Hanuman Garhi. Share stair limits before choosing the final temple sequence.

planningNotes.title: Keep the five-night split clear
planningNotes.text: The proposal is three nights in Varanasi, one in Prayagraj and one in Ayodhya. Arrival is in Varanasi and departure in Ayodhya. A return to Varanasi or onward transfer to Lucknow is additional, not hidden inside the final day.

planningNotes.title: A pilgrimage should follow your priorities
planningNotes.text: Name any essential darshan or family ceremony before the route is finalised. Rituals, priests, offerings and passes require an explicit arrangement; this sample promises none of them. Keep an extra night available if the religious purpose needs more time.

planningNotes.title: Friday changes the Sarnath order
planningNotes.text: The museum is closed on Fridays. Exchange the two full Varanasi days when needed. Check current Kashi Vishwanath electronics and security instructions close to departure, and reconfirm Ayodhya access separately.

planningNotes.title: Check steps and the final approach
planningNotes.text: Hanuman Garhi has a steep stepped approach. Ghats and boat boarding also require a suitable mobility plan. A vehicle booking does not itself establish access to the final temple entrance or riverbank.

planningNotes.title: Treat transfer ranges as estimates
planningNotes.text: Road allowances include ordinary city access and a short stop, but are not live traffic forecasts. Festivals, fog, weather and local restrictions can make them longer. Do not use a sample road estimate to book a tight onward connection.

routeContent.lead: A suggested five-day route connecting the place of the Buddha's first teaching with the Mahabodhi Temple complex at Bodh Gaya. Spend two nights in Varanasi and two in Bodh Gaya, with a dedicated transfer day between them. Gaya's Hindu pilgrimage traditions remain a separate, optional interest rather than being folded into the Buddhist visits.
routeContent.pace: Two bases; one substantial road day; time at the principal sites
routeContent.bestFor: Travellers exploring Buddhist history, pilgrims who want time at Sarnath and Mahabodhi, and visitors who prefer a focused route to an extensive temple circuit.
routeContent.season: October to March is a practical shared window for Varanasi and Bodh Gaya. Bihar Tourism gives September to April for Mahabodhi; plan outdoor visits around the actual weather and religious calendar.
highlights: A substantial Sarnath visit
Dhamek Stupa and the museum collection
Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site
Two nights in Bodh Gaya, with selected monasteries

dayPlans.title: Arrive in Varanasi and find the river
dayPlans.description: Begin with an uncomplicated arrival. Varanasi provides the base for tomorrow's Sarnath visit, and a short riverfront outing introduces the living city around it. The first evening can include aarti, but the route does not depend on reaching a ceremony straight from a flight or train.
moments: Settle into the Varanasi base
A short ghat walk
An optional evening by the Ganga

schedule.title: Keep the first hours open
schedule.text: Travel to your selected accommodation, eat and rest. If you choose an old-city address, confirm its final approach and luggage arrangements. A quiet start will make tomorrow's archaeological visit easier than adding several temples immediately after arrival.

schedule.title: Meet Varanasi at walking pace
schedule.text: Choose a short stretch of the ghats rather than trying to cover the entire riverfront. Watch everyday activity from a respectful distance and decide where to turn back according to the steps and the group's energy. Any boat outing remains a separate choice.

schedule.title: Aarti, or simply dinner
schedule.text: If the arrival leaves enough time, consider Ganga aarti at Dashashwamedh. Otherwise, have an early meal and discuss tomorrow's Sarnath sequence. Aarti is part of Varanasi's Hindu religious life; it complements the visit without being presented as a Buddhist ceremony.

dayPlans.travel: Arrival transfer depends on the specific station or airport and accommodation address.
dayPlans.walking: Optional ghat walk with steps; it can be shortened or left out after a tiring journey.

dayPlans.title: Sarnath, with time to understand what remains
dayPlans.description: Give the day to Sarnath rather than combining it with a long Varanasi temple circuit. Start with Dhamek Stupa and the excavated site, then use the museum to put the surviving sculpture and objects into context. The museum's Friday closure must be checked against the route before booking.
moments: Dhamek Stupa and the archaeological site
The Lion Capital of Ashoka in the museum
A selected monastery, only if time and access permit

schedule.title: Walk the archaeological landscape
schedule.text: Travel from Varanasi after breakfast. At Sarnath, focus on the remains associated with the place where the Buddha first taught after enlightenment. Take time at Dhamek Stupa and the excavated site; an agreed guide can help connect surviving structures with the wider history.

schedule.title: Make the museum part of the visit
schedule.text: On an open day, continue to the museum and the Lion Capital of Ashoka. Do not assume the museum follows the same hours as the outdoor site. Take a meal break, then consider a single nearby Buddhist temple or monastery if its visitor arrangements allow.

schedule.title: Return and prepare for the road
schedule.text: Head back to Varanasi before adding another major excursion. Check the next day's departure time, meal-stop preferences and luggage plan. If Sarnath falls on a Friday, revise the arrival pattern or route dates; a late museum stop on transfer day is not a dependable substitute.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: 45–75 minutes each way between central Varanasi and Sarnath; the final base and traffic may change this.
dayPlans.walking: Outdoor paths and museum galleries. Include breaks and carry only what the current site rules allow.

dayPlans.title: A travel day to Bodh Gaya
dayPlans.description: Reserve this day for the move between bases. A road journey allows planned rest stops but should not be followed by a compulsory circuit of monasteries. The main Mahabodhi visit has its own day tomorrow, so an arrival delay does not consume the centre of the journey.
moments: One main intercity journey
Planned food and comfort stops
Settle into Bodh Gaya

schedule.title: Leave after breakfast
schedule.text: Check out and begin the journey with water, a meal-stop plan and any personal needs discussed in advance. Build the day around comfortable breaks and a meal stop that suits the group. Rail may be an alternative only after its actual timetable and onward transfer are checked.

schedule.title: Arrive without another timetable to chase
schedule.text: Reach Bodh Gaya and settle into the chosen accommodation. Keep lunch flexible around the journey. After a later arrival, enjoy a straightforward check-in and an easy evening; tomorrow is reserved for the main temple visit.

schedule.title: Get your bearings locally
schedule.text: If you arrive with energy to spare, take a short orientation walk near your base and establish the next morning's approach to Mahabodhi. Otherwise, rest. Any entry on this evening is optional and follows the temple's current security and visitor arrangements.

dayPlans.overnight: Bodh Gaya · first of two nights
dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: roughly 6–8 hours by road from Varanasi with breaks. Confirm the route and timing locally; weather, roadworks and city access can extend the day.
dayPlans.walking: Minimal planned walking; an evening orientation is optional.

dayPlans.title: Mahabodhi first, then a few places chosen well
dayPlans.description: The Mahabodhi Temple complex is the day's main experience. Allow time to observe, understand the setting and sit quietly where visitors are permitted. In the afternoon, choose a small number of Buddhist temples or monasteries instead of turning a focused visit into a rapid collection of photographs.
moments: Mahabodhi Temple and the Bodhi Tree setting
Unscheduled time within the permitted visitor areas
A small selection of Bodh Gaya's monasteries

schedule.title: Give Mahabodhi a generous visit
schedule.text: Approach the UNESCO-listed complex with time for security and the current belongings arrangements. The site marks the place associated with the Buddha's enlightenment. Follow the permitted route around the temple and Bodhi Tree area, allowing quiet observation rather than a fixed photo-stop duration.

schedule.title: See another Buddhist tradition
schedule.text: After lunch and a break, select one or two local monasteries or temples that are open to visitors. The Thai or Bhutanese traditions may provide a useful contrast, depending on current access. Treat worship spaces respectfully and ask before photographing interiors or people.

schedule.title: Leave room for your own response
schedule.text: Keep the evening free for rest or a return to a place you valued, if access permits. Modest clothing, footwear removal where required and quiet conduct belong to the visit. Sitting for a while in a permitted public area can be as worthwhile as adding another stop.

dayPlans.overnight: Bodh Gaya · second of two nights
dayPlans.travel: Local journeys within Bodh Gaya; agree transport according to the selected monasteries and accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: Time on foot in the temple complex, with footwear removed where required. Share mobility concerns before fixing the route.

dayPlans.title: A quiet departure, or a separately planned Gaya visit
dayPlans.description: Let the onward connection determine this day. A final Bodh Gaya visit may suit a late departure. Gaya's Vishnupad Temple and ancestral rites belong to a different pilgrimage tradition, so add them only when they are part of your purpose and there is enough time.
moments: A flexible final Bodh Gaya morning
Optional Gaya visit with its own arrangements
Departure from the confirmed airport or station

schedule.title: Choose the priority before setting out
schedule.text: If the connection permits, return to a nearby temple or simply have breakfast before checking out. Keep luggage collection and the transfer in view. For an early flight or train, keep breakfast, checkout and the transfer as the morning's simple sequence.

schedule.title: Keep Vishnupad separate
schedule.text: For travellers with a personal reason to visit Gaya, discuss the Vishnupad area and the Phalgu river setting in advance. Verify current temple access and any ritual requirements. A pind-daan ceremony needs a dedicated window, with the officiant, location and arrangements discussed beforehand.

schedule.title: Use the exact departure point
schedule.text: Confirm whether you leave from Gaya airport, Gaya Junction or another point and plan the transfer accordingly. If a substantial ceremony or a further Bihar destination matters, extend the stay. Patna or a return to Varanasi can be planned as the next leg of a longer journey.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart the Gaya / Bodh Gaya area
dayPlans.travel: Allow roughly 30–60 minutes for a local Bodh Gaya–Gaya road leg as a planning estimate, plus visit and onward-transfer time. Reconfirm for the exact addresses.
dayPlans.walking: Optional temple approaches; access, footwear and steps vary by the chosen visit.

planningNotes.title: Check Friday before fixing the short Varanasi stay
planningNotes.text: This route has only one full Sarnath day. If it falls on Friday, the museum is closed: change the dates or add time if its collection is important. The archaeological site and the museum are separate visits.

planningNotes.title: Mahabodhi is a living religious site
planningNotes.text: Bihar Tourism advises modest dress, footwear removal and quiet conduct. Check current security, photography and electronic-device rules before leaving your accommodation. Access to a religious programme or meditation session requires a separate arrangement.

planningNotes.title: Keep Gaya and Bodh Gaya distinct
planningNotes.text: Bodh Gaya centres on Buddhist pilgrimage and Mahabodhi. Vishnupad in Gaya is a Hindu shrine associated with ancestral rites. A ritual-focused visit may need a longer stay and should be planned explicitly rather than implied by the route's destination list.

planningNotes.title: Plan the road day conservatively
planningNotes.text: The transfer ranges are editorial planning estimates, not a live map or transport timetable. Stops, weather, road conditions and the actual accommodation addresses affect the journey. Confirm the mode before booking the onward connection.

included: Two Varanasi nights and two Bodh Gaya nights, with properties and meal plans named
The agreed intercity travel mode and arrival / departure transfers
Sarnath and Bodh Gaya guiding and admission scope
Any additional Gaya visit or religious programme as a separate quoted item
excluded: Flights and rail tickets unless specifically listed
Monastery donations, offerings and personal expenses
Unconfirmed meditation, retreat, teaching or ritual participation
Patna transfers, return to Varanasi and additional destinations unless added

routeContent.kicker: A week across three different cities
routeContent.lead: A suggested seven-day route with two nights each in Lucknow, Agra and Vrindavan. Start with the Imambaras and food traditions of Awadh, continue to the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort, then finish among the temples of Braj. Two nights at each base give the main visits a full day of their own.
routeContent.pace: Three bases; two road journeys; full sightseeing days between moves
routeContent.bestFor: Travellers combining architecture and food with the devotional traditions of Braj, with time to explore beyond a single Taj Mahal stop.
routeContent.season: October to March is the preferred general sightseeing window for Agra and a practical starting point for the wider route. Check the actual weather and festival calendar before deciding daily start times.
highlights: Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza and old Lucknow
Taj Mahal and Agra Fort on a full Agra day
Two nights in Vrindavan
An optional Mathura visit without an extra hotel move

dayPlans.title: Arrive in Lucknow, with dinner as the first destination
dayPlans.description: Begin the week with one city and an easy evening. Lucknow's monuments have a full day tomorrow; today is for settling in and choosing a first meal. The food plan should follow your preferences rather than assume everyone wants the same tasting tour.
moments: Settle into your Lucknow base
A first Awadhi meal
A short local evening if arrival allows

schedule.title: Leave the main sights for tomorrow
schedule.text: Reach the chosen accommodation and allow time to unpack and rest. Confirm the next day's starting point and whether anyone wants to avoid stairs or a long market walk. An early arrival leaves time for a short local outing before dinner.

schedule.title: Take a short introduction to the city
schedule.text: If you arrive comfortably before evening, choose a local walk or a café stop near your base. Save the old-city monument cluster for a planned visit. This helps keep the first day flexible when flights, trains or city traffic alter the arrival.

schedule.title: Choose your first taste of Awadh
schedule.text: Consider an Awadhi dinner, with vegetarian preferences and any dietary requirements discussed in advance. Lucknow's food traditions include kebabs, biryani and sweets; choose a meal or tasting experience that reflects your preferences. Leave the rest of the evening easy before a full day in the old city.

dayPlans.travel: Arrival transfer set around your actual Lucknow airport or railway station and accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: An optional short walk only; the arrival evening can remain entirely at leisure.

dayPlans.title: Imambaras, Rumi Darwaza and the old city
dayPlans.description: Build the day around the architectural cluster of Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza and Chota Imambara. Grouping these visits makes more sense than repeatedly crossing the city. The maze, market walk and shopping time are choices to fit around the principal monuments.
moments: Bara Imambara
Rumi Darwaza and Chota Imambara
Time for food or chikankari shopping

schedule.title: Give Bara Imambara time
schedule.text: Begin with the main Imambara complex and its architectural spaces. If you want to explore the Bhool Bhulaiya, discuss the stairs and use an authorised guide, as the district visitor information recommends. Travellers who prefer to avoid the climb can keep their focus on the main Imambara visit.

schedule.title: Follow the neighbouring landmarks
schedule.text: Continue to Rumi Darwaza and, when the pace suits, Chota Imambara. Pause for lunch rather than treating three nearby landmarks as one uninterrupted walk. Rumi Darwaza sits between the two Imambaras, giving the visits a connected route through this part of the city.

schedule.title: Choose between the market and a relaxed meal
schedule.text: Use the remaining time for a manageable old-city walk, food or browsing chikankari textiles. Chikankari, the city's distinctive embroidery tradition, gives a textile stop a useful local focus. Return with enough time to prepare for tomorrow's road journey to Agra.

dayPlans.travel: Local city travel between the agreed monuments, market area and accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: Monument grounds and market lanes; the Bhool Bhulaiya adds stairs and should be selected separately.

dayPlans.title: Across to Agra, with an afternoon to settle
dayPlans.description: Use the Agra–Lucknow Expressway for the main road leg, with a planned meal or comfort stop. Keep the Agra arrival relaxed. Before confirming dates, check whether tomorrow is Friday: the Taj Mahal's weekly closure can change the whole order of this stay.
moments: Travel from Lucknow to Agra
A planned break on the journey
Prepare for the Taj visit

schedule.title: Make the transfer the main plan
schedule.text: Leave after breakfast and travel towards Agra. The expressway improves the connection, but door-to-door travel also includes city approaches and stops. Set a comfortable departure time and avoid attaching a tightly timed monument admission to the expected arrival.

schedule.title: Check in before choosing an extra visit
schedule.text: Settle into the Agra accommodation and take a break. An early arrival may allow a small additional outing or time to become familiar with the neighbourhood around your stay. The next day already includes two major monuments, so rest is a sensible use of the remaining afternoon.

schedule.title: Prepare for an early start
schedule.text: Confirm the Taj entry plan, approved belongings and the route from vehicle drop-off to the gate. Pack lightly and check breakfast arrangements if an early visit is chosen. If tomorrow is Friday, adjust the sequence or length of the stay before making bookings.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: approximately 5–6 hours door to door from Lucknow, including city access and a break; this is longer than the expressway-only journey.
dayPlans.walking: Minimal planned walking on the transfer day; any additional visit is optional.

dayPlans.title: The Taj Mahal, then Agra Fort
dayPlans.description: Give the Taj Mahal the first part of the day on an open date, then pause before Agra Fort. Seeing both provides a fuller introduction to Mughal Agra than a single photograph of the Taj. Keep the evening free rather than adding a distant excursion by default.
moments: Taj Mahal on an open day
A proper break between monuments
Agra Fort and its imperial setting

schedule.title: Arrive prepared for the Taj
schedule.text: An early visit can help organise the day around the heat and later crowds. Allow time for the last approach and security, and carry only permitted belongings. Photography is prohibited inside the main mausoleum; current ticket conditions should be checked before entry.

schedule.title: Change scale at Agra Fort
schedule.text: Return for breakfast or take a longer meal and rest break, depending on the start time. Continue to Agra Fort with enough energy to explore its courtyards and visitor areas. A guide and the extent of the visit can be agreed according to your interest in history.

schedule.title: Keep a little space in Agra
schedule.text: Have an unhurried evening and prepare for the next base. If another monument matters, discuss replacing part of the day rather than automatically adding Fatehpur Sikri or a long excursion. This route protects time at the two principal sites.

dayPlans.travel: Local Agra travel. The Taj's official guidance restricts polluting vehicles near the monument, so allow for the final approach from parking.
dayPlans.walking: Substantial time on foot at two monuments. Discuss the route and assistance needs; do not assume that every visitor area is equally accessible.

dayPlans.title: From Agra to Vrindavan
dayPlans.description: Move to Braj after breakfast and settle into Vrindavan before beginning temple visits. This shorter road day leaves room for rest and an introductory evening. Prem Mandir is one possible focus, with the visit arranged around its current opening and worship schedule.
moments: Travel into the Braj region
Settle into the Vrindavan base
Prem Mandir as an optional first visit

schedule.title: Make the move without a long detour
schedule.text: Leave Agra after breakfast and travel towards Vrindavan. Keep check-in and lunch as the first priorities on arrival. A detour to another destination changes the transfer day, so specify it before the route and vehicle hours are agreed.

schedule.title: Take a break and plan temple access
schedule.text: Rest at the accommodation and confirm the evening's visiting window. Discuss where a vehicle can drop the group and any final walk or local transport. The temple visits should follow current access arrangements rather than a fixed sequence copied from a standard package.

schedule.title: An introduction to Vrindavan
schedule.text: Consider Prem Mandir for the first temple visit, or choose another place that matters personally to you. Keep the outing modest after changing bases. Use the visit to become familiar with the temple grounds and the devotional atmosphere before returning for dinner.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: around 2–3 hours from Agra, including normal city access; festival diversions and the final approach can extend it.
dayPlans.walking: Temple grounds and the final approach from the agreed drop-off point; keep the first outing short.

dayPlans.title: Vrindavan first, with Mathura as a considered choice
dayPlans.description: Plan Banke Bihari around the current darshan arrangements, then take a break before deciding whether to continue to Mathura. The two places belong to the same wider Braj region, but a meaningful visit should leave time for temple queues, meals and the return journey.
moments: Banke Bihari, subject to current access
A break between temple visits
Optional Mathura and Vishram Ghat

schedule.title: Choose the darshan window carefully
schedule.text: Visit Banke Bihari when the current temple arrangements allow. Agree the approach and meeting point before entering busy lanes, and leave time for waiting. Keep the next part of the day flexible so the temple visit can take the time it needs.

schedule.title: Keep Mathura optional
schedule.text: After a meal and rest, decide whether to visit Mathura. Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi or the Yamuna-side Vishram Ghat may be considered according to interests and current access. Choose one principal Mathura stop, with time to pause beside the Yamuna if that is part of your interest.

schedule.title: Return to the same base
schedule.text: Come back to Vrindavan for the second night, allowing time for the road journey and any local restrictions. If you prefer to remain in Vrindavan throughout, use the afternoon for another chosen temple and a shorter evening. The overnight plan stays the same.

dayPlans.travel: If Mathura is chosen, use roughly 45–75 minutes each way as a planning allowance; exact destinations and crowd controls matter.
dayPlans.walking: Busy temple lanes, queues and possible riverfront steps. Keep the optional Mathura programme separate from the morning's physical demands.

dayPlans.title: Leave Braj at a comfortable pace
dayPlans.description: Finish with breakfast and a departure plan based on the actual onward ticket. A nearby visit may fit a late departure, but this final morning is not a substitute for another full day in Braj. Decide the end point before confirming transport.
moments: A flexible final morning
Check out without another major excursion
Depart from the agreed connection

schedule.title: Keep one local possibility
schedule.text: If time allows, return to a temple close to your accommodation or take an easy breakfast. Keep the outing short enough to collect luggage and check out comfortably. The day can equally remain free of sightseeing after a week on the road.

schedule.title: Confirm where the next journey begins
schedule.text: Check the precise railway station or airport on your onward ticket. Mathura, Agra and Delhi are different transfer plans with different time requirements. Set the transfer according to the exact endpoint before confirming the final day's pickup.

schedule.title: Travel with the right allowance
schedule.text: Set the pickup and final approach with current local advice, particularly around religious dates. Any extra transfer should appear in the written quote. If another Braj destination remains important, extend the route rather than relying on spare time before a connection.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart the Vrindavan / Mathura area
dayPlans.travel: Departure transfer to be quoted from the exact accommodation to the confirmed connection; no Delhi transfer is assumed.
dayPlans.walking: An optional short local visit only; no major walk is required on departure day.

planningNotes.title: Work around the Taj's Friday closure
planningNotes.text: The Taj Mahal is closed to general sightseeing on Fridays. If the full Agra day is Friday, move the Taj visit only when the actual arrival or departure allows it; otherwise change the nights or dates. Agra Fort is not a substitute for a promised Taj visit.

planningNotes.title: Know the Taj approach and belongings rules
planningNotes.text: The official visitor guidance restricts polluting vehicles near the monument, prohibits photography inside the main mausoleum and advises travelling without large bags. Confirm the current rules and ticket conditions before your visit.

planningNotes.title: Choose the maze rather than assume it
planningNotes.text: Lucknow's district guidance describes stairs into the Bhool Bhulaiya and recommends an authorised guide. It can be left out while retaining the Imambara visit. Tell the planner about stair concerns before the sightseeing scope is fixed.

planningNotes.title: Braj follows the temples' own routines
planningNotes.text: Darshan windows, queues and local vehicle access can change, especially around festivals. Check the current arrangements for each temple and keep Mathura optional. No special access, ceremony or event is guaranteed.

planningNotes.title: Three bases and realistic road allowances
planningNotes.text: The proposed split is two nights in each city. Road ranges are editorial estimates including ordinary access and short breaks, not live forecasts. Exact properties, local controls and weather can change them.

included: Six nights: two each in Lucknow, Agra and Vrindavan, with properties specified
The two intercity legs and agreed local / arrival / departure transport
Guide arrangements, monument admissions and temple visit scope

excluded: Flights or rail tickets unless the quote adds them
Unlisted meals, shopping, donations and personal expenses

Additional destinations, nights or transfers outside the agreed programme

routeContent.lead: A suggested three-day stay that gives Ayodhya a full day between arrival and departure. Plan Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi and Kanak Bhawan around your priorities, with an evening beside the Sarayu. Staying in one base leaves room for queues and rest without adding a long intercity transfer.
routeContent.pace: One base; one full temple day; flexible arrival and departure
routeContent.bestFor: A focused Ayodhya pilgrimage, families who want two nights in one place, and travellers whose main priority is darshan rather than a multi-city circuit.
routeContent.season: Suggested planning window: October to March. Ram Navami and Deepotsav visits need a separate crowd, access and accommodation plan rather than the ordinary-day schedule below.
highlights: A full day for your chosen Ayodhya temples
Ram Mandir and Kanak Bhawan
Hanuman Garhi when the steps suit your group
Ram Ki Paidi and the Sarayu riverfront

dayPlans.title: Arrive in Ayodhya and settle by the Sarayu
dayPlans.description: Keep arrival day light and use the riverfront as an introduction to the city. Two nights allow the principal temple programme to wait until tomorrow. An evening at Ram Ki Paidi is a possibility, not a reason to rush directly from a flight or train.
moments: Settle into the Ayodhya base
Confirm the next day's temple priorities
An evening around Ram Ki Paidi

schedule.title: Confirm the approach to your stay
schedule.text: Reach the selected accommodation and allow time for a meal and rest. Discuss the final vehicle drop-off and luggage arrangements if access is restricted near the property. If you arrive via Lucknow rather than Ayodhya, that road transfer needs its own allowance and quote.

schedule.title: Plan tomorrow around what matters
schedule.text: Choose the main darshan and whether Hanuman Garhi's stairs suit the group. Confirm the current entry and belongings instructions before setting departure times. This is also the moment to explain any family tradition or particular temple that should take priority over the sample route.

schedule.title: Begin at the riverfront
schedule.text: If the arrival permits, visit Ram Ki Paidi, the series of ghats beside the Sarayu. Keep the first walk short and identify the return meeting point. Follow the length of the riverfront walk according to the group's energy, then return for dinner and a relaxed evening.

dayPlans.travel: Local arrival transfer from your confirmed Ayodhya airport or railway station; travel from Lucknow is a separate arrangement.
dayPlans.walking: A short ghat approach with steps; the evening can be omitted if the arrival is tiring.

dayPlans.title: A full day for Ram Mandir and the temple town
dayPlans.description: Give the main darshan a generous window and fit the remaining temples around it. Hanuman Garhi and Kanak Bhawan add different experiences, but the order should follow current access and the group's own religious priorities. Keep a meal and rest break between outings.
moments: Ram Mandir, subject to current entry arrangements
Hanuman Garhi if the stepped approach suits
Kanak Bhawan and a proper afternoon break

schedule.title: Make the principal darshan the priority
schedule.text: Set the morning around Ram Mandir, allowing time for security, the approach and waiting. Some travellers prefer to visit Hanuman Garhi first; discuss that preference before fixing the order. Keep the meal and afternoon visit flexible so the main darshan can take the time it needs.

schedule.title: Pause, then visit Kanak Bhawan
schedule.text: Take a meal and return for a break before another temple visit. Kanak Bhawan is dedicated to Rama and Sita and offers a further focus within the temple town. Match the visit to its current open window rather than assuming continuous access throughout the afternoon.

schedule.title: Keep the last outing optional
schedule.text: If Hanuman Garhi remains a priority and the group can manage the steep steps, place it where the day's arrangements allow. Otherwise, revisit the riverfront or enjoy a quiet evening. The full day leaves room to return to the place that matters most to you.

dayPlans.travel: Local transport and final walking approaches depend on current city access controls and the selected accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: Queues and temple lanes; Hanuman Garhi adds substantial steep steps. Choose it separately according to the group's comfort.

dayPlans.title: One final local visit, then depart
dayPlans.description: Use the final morning according to your actual connection. A nearby riverfront or temple visit may fit a late departure, while an early train or flight calls for a straightforward checkout. Keep the flexible time for something personally meaningful instead of another long list of stops.
moments: A flexible last morning
Optional Nageshwarnath near Ram Ki Paidi
Departure from the confirmed station or airport

schedule.title: Return to the river, if time allows
schedule.text: After breakfast, consider a short return to Ram Ki Paidi or Nageshwarnath Temple in that area. Choose one nearby outing and check its current visiting arrangements. Do not commit to a cross-city excursion before collecting luggage and leaving for a connection.

schedule.title: Leave time for checkout and access
schedule.text: Return to the accommodation, collect belongings and confirm the pickup point. The same street may have different vehicle access at different times, so use current local advice. If you prefer another darshan, discuss whether a later departure or an extra night is the better plan.

schedule.title: Finish at the agreed endpoint
schedule.text: Travel to the exact Ayodhya airport or railway station on your ticket. An onward road journey to Lucknow, Prayagraj or Varanasi is an extension to specify separately. Leave a comfortable margin for the final approach to your station or airport.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart Ayodhya
dayPlans.travel: Departure transfer to the exact booked connection; no intercity return is assumed.
dayPlans.walking: Optional short local visit; otherwise only the approach required for departure.

planningNotes.title: Two nights protect the main temple day
planningNotes.text: The suggested stay is two nights in Ayodhya. Keep the full day between arrival and departure for the principal visits; an early arrival or late departure is useful flexibility, not guaranteed sightseeing time.

planningNotes.title: Check the current temple arrangements
planningNotes.text: Check current Ram Mandir and other temple instructions for your dates. Passes, religious services, queues and belongings rules are separate operational details. No VIP access, fixed waiting time or special ceremony is promised here.

planningNotes.title: Discuss Hanuman Garhi's stairs
planningNotes.text: Official tourism information describes a steep stepped approach. Let walking and stair preferences shape the visit rather than assuming that every member of the group will follow the same temple sequence.

planningNotes.title: Festival visits are a different plan
planningNotes.text: Ram Navami and Deepotsav bring a different pattern of gatherings and arrangements. Confirm dates and current local guidance before choosing accommodation and transport. Ordinary-day timings should not be reused automatically.

excluded: Flights or trains unless added to the quote

routeContent.kicker: Three days in the city of Awadh
routeContent.lead: A suggested three-day Lucknow stay with two nights in one base. Give Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza and Chota Imambara a full day, with time for Awadhi food and chikankari. A later departure can add the Residency and its account of 1857 without turning the city break into a rushed monument circuit.
routeContent.pace: One base; a full old-city day; an optional history visit before departure
routeContent.bestFor: A short break built around architecture, food and textiles, or travellers who want to explore Lucknow properly before continuing elsewhere.
routeContent.season: Suggested planning window: October to March for a walking-led city break. Set outdoor visits around the day's weather and check monument arrangements before fixing the sequence.
highlights: Bara Imambara and the optional Bhool Bhulaiya
Rumi Darwaza and Chota Imambara
Awadhi food and time for chikankari
The Residency if your departure allows

dayPlans.title: Arrive, settle in and choose an Awadhi dinner
dayPlans.description: Start your Lucknow break with an easy arrival and a first meal. The principal monuments have a full day tomorrow, so a delayed connection does not spoil the route. An early arrival leaves room for a short local outing rather than another compulsory circuit.
moments: Settle into your Lucknow base
A first Awadhi meal
A short local evening if arrival allows

schedule.title: Settle into one base for two nights
schedule.text: Reach the chosen accommodation, unpack and rest. Confirm the next day's starting point and tell the planner about any concerns with stairs or a longer market walk. The stay is designed around one base, so there is no need to repack before exploring the city.

schedule.title: Consider a short Hazratganj outing
schedule.text: If the arrival gives you time, explore a manageable stretch of Hazratganj or stop for tea nearby. Shopping can be as brief as a look at the textiles. Keep a longer old-city walk for tomorrow, when it can be combined with the monument visits.

schedule.title: Make food a personal choice
schedule.text: Choose an Awadhi meal according to your interests and dietary preferences. A restaurant reservation or guided tasting can be discussed separately. Kebabs, biryani and sweets are part of the city's food traditions; vegetarian choices and personal favourites can shape the meal. Keep the remaining evening easy.

dayPlans.travel: Arrival transfer set around your actual Lucknow airport or railway station and accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: An optional short walk only; the arrival evening can remain entirely at leisure.

dayPlans.title: Imambaras, Rumi Darwaza and the old city
dayPlans.description: Build the day around the architectural cluster of Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza and Chota Imambara. Grouping these visits makes more sense than repeatedly crossing the city. The maze, market walk and shopping time are choices to fit around the principal monuments.
moments: Bara Imambara
Rumi Darwaza and Chota Imambara
Time for food or chikankari shopping

schedule.title: Give Bara Imambara time
schedule.text: Begin with the main Imambara complex and its architectural spaces. If you want to explore the Bhool Bhulaiya, discuss the stairs and use an authorised guide, as the district visitor information recommends. Travellers who prefer to avoid the climb can keep their focus on the main Imambara visit.

schedule.title: Follow the neighbouring landmarks
schedule.text: Continue to Rumi Darwaza and, when the pace suits, Chota Imambara. Pause for lunch rather than treating three nearby landmarks as one uninterrupted walk. Rumi Darwaza sits between the two Imambaras, giving the visits a connected route through this part of the city.

schedule.title: Food, textiles or simply an easy evening
schedule.text: Choose a short old-city market visit for chikankari, a meal, or time back at the accommodation. Shopping is optional and should suit your interest rather than a seller's itinerary. If a textile workshop visit is requested, its availability and any fee need separate confirmation.

dayPlans.travel: Local city travel between the agreed monuments, market area and accommodation.
dayPlans.walking: Monument grounds and market lanes; the Bhool Bhulaiya adds stairs and should be selected separately.

dayPlans.title: The Residency, if the departure leaves room
dayPlans.description: A later departure makes space for the Residency, a different historical chapter from the previous day's Nawabi architecture. Its remains and the 1857 Memorial Museum should be visited with time to read and understand the site. An early connection means leaving this visit for a longer stay.
moments: Optional Residency visit
The 1857 Memorial Museum when open
Depart from your confirmed Lucknow connection

schedule.title: Choose the Residency over several quick stops
schedule.text: After breakfast, consider the Residency's grounds and ruined buildings if the departure schedule permits. The site is associated with the events of 1857. Give the visit a clear time window and avoid fitting several other monuments into the same morning.

schedule.title: Check the museum separately
schedule.text: The 1857 Memorial Museum sits within the complex and provides further historical context. Confirm its current open day and hours before relying on it. If it is closed or time is short, decide whether the grounds alone suit your interest rather than implying access to both.

schedule.title: Return for luggage and leave comfortably
schedule.text: Allow time to return, check out and reach the exact station or airport on your ticket. If the transfer window is tight, keep the entire morning free. A food walk or shopping session that needs longer is a reason to extend the visit, not compress the departure.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart Lucknow
dayPlans.travel: Local sightseeing and departure transfer, planned around the precise accommodation and booked connection.
dayPlans.walking: The optional Residency visit involves time outdoors across the grounds; choose the extent according to the group and weather.

planningNotes.title: One base, with time for food and textiles
planningNotes.text: Two nights are proposed in Lucknow. Food and textile stops should follow your preferences. A workshop, tasting, named restaurant or particular guide requires an explicit arrangement and cannot be assumed from the destination description.

planningNotes.title: Choose the Bhool Bhulaiya separately
planningNotes.text: The district's visitor information describes stairs into the maze and recommends an authorised guide. Keep it optional when steps are a concern; the rest of the Imambara programme can still be planned around your interests.

planningNotes.title: Match the Residency to the departure
planningNotes.text: The grounds and the 1857 Memorial Museum are related but distinct parts of the visit. Verify current access and museum hours, and only include the outing when there is a sensible margin before your onward connection.

planningNotes.title: Set the food plan before the walk
planningNotes.text: Share vegetarian preferences, food interests and dietary requirements before any tasting is arranged. No meal or restaurant is included until the written proposal states it, and shopping remains entirely optional.

included: Two Lucknow nights with named accommodation and meal plan
Agreed arrival, departure and city transport
Monument admissions and guiding scope, including any maze visit
A food experience, workshop or restaurant reservation only if specifically arranged
excluded: Flights or rail tickets unless listed
Meals and tastings outside the confirmed plan
Textiles, shopping, gratuities and personal expenses
Unlisted excursions or access to closed visitor areas

routeContent.lead: A suggested four-day route with two nights in Agra and one in Vrindavan. Give the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort a full day, then move into Braj for a temple-focused evening and morning. The short route concentrates on these two bases; Mathura or further Braj destinations can be added when your onward plans allow.
routeContent.pace: Two bases; one short intercity leg; a full day in Agra
routeContent.bestFor: Travellers combining a first Taj Mahal visit with Vrindavan, or a short northern India trip that balances architecture and pilgrimage.
routeContent.season: October to March is the preferred general sightseeing season for Agra. Match Vrindavan visits to the current temple and festival calendar, and plan the route around the Taj Mahal's Friday closure.
highlights: Taj Mahal and Agra Fort
Two nights in Agra before changing base
A Vrindavan evening and temple morning
One direct move from Agra into Braj

dayPlans.title: Arrive in Agra and prepare for tomorrow's monuments
dayPlans.description: Begin with an easy Agra arrival and leave the Taj Mahal for a full visiting day. If you arrive early and want a smaller first outing, the Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah is an option across the Yamuna. Keep the visit flexible around the actual arrival and time to settle in.
moments: Settle into the Agra base
Optional Itimad-ud-Daulah visit
Prepare for the Taj's entry arrangements

schedule.title: Start with check-in and a meal
schedule.text: Reach the chosen accommodation and rest before deciding whether to go out. Confirm the actual airport or railway station for the arrival transfer. A road arrival from Delhi is a separate journey with its own allowance; it is not automatically included in an itinerary starting in Agra.

schedule.title: An optional smaller monument
schedule.text: If the schedule permits, consider the Tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah for its marble work and riverside setting. The Agra district identifies it as a separate monument across the Yamuna. Leave it out after a late arrival rather than rushing there immediately before closing.

schedule.title: Prepare for the full Agra day
schedule.text: Check the next morning's entry plan, permitted belongings and final approach to the Taj gate. Keep the evening relaxed. If tomorrow is Friday, the Taj visit must move to a workable open day or the stay must change before reservations are made.

dayPlans.travel: Arrival transfer within Agra as agreed; Delhi road transfers require a separate plan.
dayPlans.walking: Optional monument grounds only; the arrival day can remain free of sightseeing.

dayPlans.title: The Taj Mahal, then Agra Fort
dayPlans.description: Give the Taj Mahal the first part of the day on an open date, then pause before Agra Fort. Seeing both provides a fuller introduction to Mughal Agra than a single photograph of the Taj. Keep the evening free rather than adding a distant excursion by default.
moments: Taj Mahal on an open day
A proper break between monuments
Agra Fort and its imperial setting

schedule.title: Arrive prepared for the Taj
schedule.text: An early visit can help organise the day around the heat and later crowds. Allow time for the last approach and security, and carry only permitted belongings. Photography is prohibited inside the main mausoleum; current ticket conditions should be checked before entry.

schedule.title: Change scale at Agra Fort
schedule.text: Return for breakfast or take a longer meal and rest break, depending on the start time. Continue to Agra Fort with enough energy to explore its courtyards and visitor areas. A guide and the extent of the visit can be agreed according to your interest in history.

schedule.title: Keep a little space in Agra
schedule.text: Have an unhurried evening and prepare for the next base. If another monument matters, discuss replacing part of the day rather than automatically adding Fatehpur Sikri or a long excursion. This route protects time at the two principal sites.

dayPlans.travel: Local Agra travel. The Taj's official guidance restricts polluting vehicles near the monument, so allow for the final approach from parking.
dayPlans.walking: Substantial time on foot at two monuments. Discuss the route and assistance needs; do not assume that every visitor area is equally accessible.

dayPlans.title: From Agra to Vrindavan
dayPlans.description: After two nights in Agra, move to Vrindavan and take time to settle in. Use the evening for one chosen temple, such as Prem Mandir, with the timing checked locally. The following morning remains available for Banke Bihari if it fits your onward connection.
moments: Travel into the Braj region
Settle into the Vrindavan base
Prem Mandir as an optional first visit

schedule.title: Make the move without a long detour
schedule.text: Leave Agra after breakfast and travel towards Vrindavan. Keep check-in and lunch as the first priorities on arrival. A detour to another destination changes the transfer day, so specify it before the route and vehicle hours are agreed.

schedule.title: Take a break and plan temple access
schedule.text: Rest at the accommodation and confirm the evening's visiting window. Discuss where a vehicle can drop the group and any final walk or local transport. The temple visits should follow current access arrangements rather than a fixed sequence copied from a standard package.

schedule.title: An introduction to Vrindavan
schedule.text: Consider Prem Mandir for the first temple visit, or choose another place that matters personally to you. Keep the outing modest after changing bases. Use the visit to become familiar with the temple grounds and the devotional atmosphere before returning for dinner.

dayPlans.travel: Planning allowance: around 2–3 hours from Agra, including normal city access; festival diversions and the final approach can extend it.
dayPlans.walking: Temple grounds and the final approach from the agreed drop-off point; keep the first outing short.

dayPlans.title: A Vrindavan morning before travelling onward
dayPlans.description: Use the final morning for your principal Vrindavan temple visit, with Banke Bihari as the proposed focus. A later departure is preferable when darshan matters. Mathura is an optional extension to discuss, not another full programme automatically squeezed in before a train or flight.
moments: Banke Bihari if current access and departure allow
A meal and time to collect luggage
Depart from the agreed Braj connection

schedule.title: Put darshan ahead of extra stops
schedule.text: Plan Banke Bihari around the temple's current visiting arrangements, allowing for the approach and queue. Agree a meeting point before entering busy lanes. Leave a generous window for darshan, with a later onward connection or another night if the visit needs more time.

schedule.title: Keep the rest of the morning useful
schedule.text: Take breakfast or an early meal, collect belongings and check out. If you want to visit Mathura's Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi or Vishram Ghat, discuss the additional visit and travel time before fixing transport. Choose an additional stop only when there is time for the visit as well as the journey to the station.

schedule.title: Leave from the exact booked endpoint
schedule.text: Travel to the station or airport named on your onward ticket. Mathura, Agra and Delhi require different allowances and costs. The four-day route ends in the Braj area; any further road transfer needs to be written into the final proposal.

dayPlans.overnight: No overnight stay proposed · depart the Vrindavan / Mathura area
dayPlans.travel: Final transfer is set from the confirmed accommodation to the booked connection; Delhi is not an assumed endpoint.
dayPlans.walking: Temple lanes and standing in queues. Keep additional visits conditional on energy and time.

planningNotes.title: Friday determines the Agra order
planningNotes.text: The Taj Mahal is closed to general sightseeing on Fridays. This route needs a workable open-day visit: change the order only when arrival and transfer times permit, otherwise adjust the dates or add a night.

planningNotes.title: Three nights, two bases
planningNotes.text: The proposed split is two nights in Agra and one in Vrindavan. A Delhi arrival or departure is extra travel to plan explicitly. More time in Mathura, Barsana or other Braj places calls for an extension rather than a longer checklist.

planningNotes.title: Read the monument rules before leaving
planningNotes.text: The Taj's official visitor guidance covers the final approach, prohibited belongings and the photography restriction inside the main mausoleum. Check the current rules and carry only what is permitted; ticket and guide arrangements must be stated separately.

planningNotes.title: Protect the final temple morning
planningNotes.text: Banke Bihari's current darshan arrangements and local access determine the final morning. Choose a suitable onward connection, and allow for queues. The Agra–Vrindavan road allowance is a planning estimate, not a live traffic promise.
